In [[geometry]], a '''truncated 120-cell''' is a [[uniform 4-polytope]] formed as the [[Truncation (geometry)|truncation]] of the regular [[120-cell]]. 

There are three truncations, including a [[bitruncation]], and a tritruncation, which creates the ''truncated 600-cell''.

[[File:Truncated hecatonicosachoron net.png|thumb|right|[[Net (polyhedron)|Net]]]]
The '''truncated 120-cell''' or '''truncated hecatonicosachoron''' is a [[uniform 4-polytope]], constructed by a uniform [[Truncation (geometry)|truncation]] of the [[Convex regular 4-polytope|regular]] [[120-cell]] [[4-polytope]]. 

It is made of 120 [[Truncated dodecahedron|truncated dodecahedral]] and 600 [[Tetrahedron|tetrahedral]] cells. It has 3120 faces: 2400 being [[triangle]]s and 720 being [[decagon]]s. There are 4800 edges of two types: 3600 shared by three truncated dodecahedra and 1200 are shared by two truncated dodecahedra and one tetrahedron. Each vertex has 3 truncated dodecahedra and one tetrahedron around it. Its [[vertex figure]] is an equilateral triangular pyramid.

=== Alternate names ===
* Truncated 120-cell ([[Norman Johnson (mathematician)|Norman W. Johnson]])
** Tuncated hecatonicosachoron / Truncated dodecacontachoron / Truncated polydodecahedron
* Truncated-icosahedral hexacosihecatonicosachoron (Acronym thi) (George Olshevsky, and Jonathan Bowers)<ref>Klitizing, (o3o3x5x - thi)</ref>

[[File:Hexacosihecatonicosachoron net.png|thumb|right|[[Net (polyhedron)|Net]]]]
The '''bitruncated 120-cell''' or '''hexacosihecatonicosachoron''' is a [[uniform 4-polytope]]. It has 720 cells: 120 [[Truncated icosahedron|truncated icosahedra]], and 600 [[Truncated tetrahedron|truncated tetrahedra]]. Its [[vertex figure]] is a digonal [[disphenoid]], with two truncated icosahedra and two truncated tetrahedra around it.

=== Alternate names ===
* Bitruncated 120-cell / Bitruncated 600-cell ([[Norman Johnson (mathematician)|Norman W. Johnson]])
** Bitruncated hecatonicosachoron / Bitruncated hexacosichoron / Bitruncated polydodecahedron / Bitruncated polytetrahedron
* Truncated-icosahedral hexacosihecatonicosachoron (Acronym Xhi) (George Olshevsky, and Jonathan Bowers)<ref>Klitizing, (o3x3x5o - xhi)</ref>

[[File:Truncated hexacosichoron net.png|thumb|right|[[Net (polyhedron)|Net]]]]
The '''truncated 600-cell''' or '''truncated hexacosichoron''' is a [[uniform 4-polytope]]. It is derived from the [[600-cell]] by [[truncation (geometry)|truncation]]. It has 720 cells: 120 [[icosahedron|icosahedra]] and 600 [[Truncated tetrahedron|truncated tetrahedra]]. Its [[vertex figure]] is a [[pentagonal pyramid]], with one icosahedron on the base, and 5 truncated tetrahedra around the sides.

=== Alternate names ===
* Truncated 600-cell ([[Norman Johnson (mathematician)|Norman W. Johnson]])
* Truncated hexacosichoron (Acronym tex) (George Olshevsky, and Jonathan Bowers)<ref>Klitizing, (x3x3o5o - tex)</ref>
* Truncated tetraplex (Conway)

=== Structure ===

The truncated 600-cell consists of 600 [[truncated tetrahedron|truncated tetrahedra]] and 120 [[icosahedron|icosahedra]]. The truncated tetrahedral cells are joined to each other via their hexagonal faces, and to the icosahedral cells via their triangular faces. Each icosahedron is surrounded by 20 truncated tetrahedra.
